scenarios.invocation: XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<temporary symlink to local/nvim> nvim --headless '+Lazy! install sidekick.nvim' '+qa'

scenarios.name: actual Sidekick terminal starts and closes Codex
real Neovim PTY command surface
scenarios.invocation: expect -> env -u NVIM TERM=xterm-256color nvim -u .local-setup/ai-tooling/sidekick/pty/init.lua fixture.lua -> :lua require("sidekick.cli").toggle({name="codex",focus=true})
scenarios.observable: raw terminal stream contains the actual Neovim session and Sidekick toggle command; no model prompt text was sent
scenarios.limitation: The available PTY emulator does not answer Neovim's DSR color request and no xterm.js web-terminal capture helper exists in this workspace, so this is an ANSI capture rather than a screenshot. The separate live-session scenario above proves process startup and closure.

scenarios.name: operating-manual synchronization and lifecycle instructions
scenarios.invocation: rg -n 'apply-config|lazy-lock|cli close|tmux' menual/ai-tools/sidekick.md; git diff --no-index --check /dev/null menual/ai-tools/sidekick.md
scenarios.observable: the Korean manual requires reviewed apply-config before an isolated Sidekick update and explicitly syncs the live lockfile back to the repository; removal backs up and deletes both source and live config because apply-config does not delete stale targets; hide/toggle retains a terminal process, while cli close or Neovim exit ends it; health warnings may include tmux despite mux=false
